acceptanceCriteria: Each provider test identity has a separately encrypted profile, immutable account alias, domain allowlist, generation, retention, and health state
Enrollment records human provenance and provider/session health without recording password, cookie, TOTP seed, passkey private material, or recovery code
Profiles mount only into isolated browser runners and are absent from model context, prompts, job JSON, logs, API bodies, screenshots, and authority rows
Cross-provider, cross-account, cross-workspace, and non-allowlisted origin use fails before navigation
Deleting or quarantining a profile revokes active leases and preserves redacted audit evidence
userStories.description: Implement BrowserSessionBroker as a Rorca AuthorityProviderAdapter for dedicated external test identities. Store encrypted domain-bound profile artifacts and SecretStore references with provider, account alias, allowlisted origins, enrollment provenance, health state, generation, retention, and destruction policy; never store cookies or TOTP seeds in authority rows. Human enrollment completes login/MFA/passkey on an operator-controlled surface. Use core ProviderBinding/receipt storage; no plaintext child table or customer identity dependency.
userStories.title: Dedicated browser profiles keep external identity secrets outside model context

acceptanceCriteria: Lease issuance rejects unhealthy/stale profiles, wrong workspace/provider, broadened origins/actions, expired grants, and concurrent use beyond policy
One lease mounts one profile generation into one isolated runner and exposes no raw profile file to the model
Network navigation outside the exact provider/MCP allowlist fails and records a redacted security event
Revocation terminates the runner, invalidates further actions, clears ephemeral state, and applies the profile retention policy
Crash or lost runner heartbeat reconciles session/provider health before the profile can be leased again
userStories.description: Implement browser.session.request, use, revoke, and reconcile under the core grant/lease state machine. Bind each lease to run, story, purpose, profile generation, allowed origins/actions, maximum concurrent runner count, expiry, evidence contract, and destruction/preservation policy. Launch a fresh isolated browser runner with constrained network/filesystem/artifact access. Revocation terminates use and clears ephemeral state; uncertain termination reconciles before reuse.
userStories.title: Expiring browser leases isolate one run, purpose, profile, and domain set

acceptanceCriteria: Each supported step-up state produces a typed request and durable run wait rather than a narrative block or story timeout
The operator can complete or cancel the step on a takeover surface while model input and automation are suspended
MFA, passkey, CAPTCHA, account lock, and provider anti-automation controls cannot be bypassed or marked complete without observed provider state
Restart during the wait preserves exact browser/profile/run position and resumes once only after health revalidation
Denied, cancelled, expired, unhealthy, or policy-prohibited steps revoke the lease and return a typed terminal/retryable outcome
userStories.description: Detect login expiry, consent, MFA, passkey, CAPTCHA, account lock, and provider step-up states as structured authentication requests. Transition the run to WAITING_FOR_AUTHENTICATION with the exact provider/profile/purpose/evidence and a separate expiry; stop story timeout. Present an operator takeover surface that never exposes model control during the human step. Resume once after health revalidation. Enforce documented provider terms and anti-automation constraints; never bypass, auto-solve, or extract secrets.
userStories.title: Step-up authentication pauses durably for the human operator

acceptanceCriteria: The real Claude consumer surface completes fixture installation/connection, consent, deterministic tool call, refresh, revocation, and verified post-revocation failure
Evidence records timestamps, UI observations, redacted network metadata, MCP result hashes, and revocation proof without cookies or tokens
The conformance fixture accepts only the bounded test identity/client and harmless deterministic tool contract
Session and OAuth leases are revoked or verified expired and the profile is preserved/quarantined/destroyed according to policy
The journey requires no Categoric/Cashflow-App MCP server, OAuth client, code, account, or workspace
userStories.description: Create a disposable Rorca-owned MCP conformance fixture with deterministic OAuth consent, one harmless tool, refresh, and revocation endpoints; it is test infrastructure, not Categoric. Through a dedicated Claude consumer test identity and leased browser runner, perform real install/connect, consent, tool invocation, refresh, revoke, and post-revocation failure. Capture redacted screenshots, accessibility snapshots, network metadata, MCP result hashes, provider/session state, and revocation proof in one ExecutionReceipt.
userStories.title: Claude onboarding proves a real MCP consumer journey on a Rorca-owned fixture

acceptanceCriteria: The real ChatGPT consumer surface completes fixture installation/connection, consent, deterministic tool call, refresh, revocation, and verified post-revocation failure
Evidence contains the same required classes as Claude and records explicit provider-specific differences
Claude and ChatGPT accounts, profiles, leases, cookies, and OAuth grants remain isolated and cannot be interchanged
No cookie, token, TOTP, password, passkey material, or recovery code appears in model context or retained evidence
The journey requires no Categoric/Cashflow-App MCP server, OAuth client, code, account, or workspace
userStories.description: Run the same Rorca-owned MCP conformance fixture journey through a separately enrolled ChatGPT consumer test identity and profile. Preserve provider-specific UI differences while requiring equivalent install/connect, consent, tool, refresh, revoke, and post-revocation observations and the same redaction/provenance classes. Do not reuse the Claude profile, lease, cookies, account, or OAuth grant.
userStories.title: ChatGPT onboarding produces evidence equivalent to the Claude journey

acceptanceCriteria: Crash injection resumes or reconciles once without duplicate onboarding, duplicate OAuth grants, orphan runners, or untracked sessions
Cookie, TOTP, password, passkey, token, cross-domain/profile/provider, replay, revoked-session, takeover-automation, and network-escape attempts all fail
Evidence tampering changes the receipt digest and prevents acceptance
Every injected failure leaves the dedicated provider account healthy or quarantined with an explicit operator recovery action
Disabling the broker revokes leases, terminates runners, blocks new requests, preserves receipts, and leaves no Categoric/Cashflow-App dependency
userStories.description: Inject crashes at enrollment handoff, lease issue, navigation, consent, tool call, refresh, revoke, and receipt settlement. Attempt prompt extraction of cookies/TOTP/tokens, cross-domain/profile/provider use, expired/replayed lease, revoked-session reuse, automation during takeover, evidence tampering, and network escape. Qualify only dedicated test identities. Rollout remains experimental and off by default; rollback revokes leases, kills runners, quarantines profiles, disables the broker, and retains redacted receipts. Non-goals are personal accounts, general browsing, CAPTCHA solving, credential export, provider-policy circumvention, and unattended production browser automation.
userStories.title: Browser-session attacks and crashes leave accounts healthy and evidence complete
